text.p: Italian bond futures closed above the day's lows but well down from a record high for the December LIFFE contract of 126.43 reached in early trade as investors took profits after the surge in prices of the last two days.

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi gave a late boost to the market when he told a news conference that the latest European Union forecasts confirmed that Italy could join a single currency from the start.
His reiteration of the government's commitment to take the lira back into the ERM currency grid by the end of the month was also a factor supporting the market.
Earlier some of the wind was knocked out of the market when the European Monetary Institute said Germany, France and Italy needed to make sustained efforts to the meet the EMU criteria.
The EU had also said it saw Italy's deficit/GDP ratio at 3.3 percent in 1997 but added it might fall further.

"The market over-extended itself yesterday and we saw profit-taking today," said Andrew Carless, a dealer at Fimat Futures in London. "The market is now looking for a pointer both politically and technically."
One dealer said BTP futures could climb higher if the lira breaks through the 1,000 lire barrier against the mark.

"It's still a currency play," said a London futures dealer. "People will try to see where the Bank of Italy is so they can point out where the lira's mid-point in the ERM is going to be." Milan newsroom +392-66102321
